title: Polynesian settlement of New Zealand
summary: Radiocarbon dates on Pacific rat bones and rat-gnawed seeds show the rat reached both main islands of New Zealand around AD 1280, a millennium later than earlier estimates. Because the rat travelled with voyagers, this marks the first human arrival, making it the point at which human history in New Zealand begins.

uncertainty.note: Wilmshurst et al. (2008) give about 1280 AD for introduction of the Pacific rat; a Landcare Research summary states 1280-1300 AD as the earliest evidence. Dates are calibrated radiocarbon ages. Not to be confused with the 2011 East Polynesia chronology in the linked record.

as_recorded.value: Pacific rat was introduced to both main islands of New Zealand ≈1280 A.D.
earliest evidence for human colonization is about 1280-1300 AD

where.historical_name: Aotearoa / New Zealand before first settlement; no recorded name at that date

importance.justification: Marks the first human arrival in New Zealand, one of the last large lands to be settled by people.
